column1: # himmel uninstall path manifest (HIMMEL-3058) — the ONE list of every surface
# scripts/uninstall.sh acts on. The uninstaller READS this file: the removal
# targets, the code-vs-state class that gates --purge-state, the printed
# footprint and the post-run read-back all come from here, so a path cannot be
# touched without being listed (a re-derived list is how paths get missed).
# scripts/uninstall.ps1 keeps its own targets and does NOT read this file; only
# its -PurgeState gating is checked (source-level) by scripts/test-uninstall-ux.sh
# P1 — keep the two in step by hand until it reads the manifest.
# Columns, TAB-separated ('-' = not applicable; blank/# lines ignored):
#   id       stable name, referenced by uninstall.sh
#   class    code  = himmel's own code/wiring/cache — removed by default
#            state = operator data — kept unless --purge-state is passed
#            keep  = never touched by uninstall, listed so the footprint is complete
#   surface  which of the machine's surfaces this lives on
#   kind     dir | settings | githooks | process | jobs | plugins | marketplaces | file
#   env      env var that overrides the path (tests, non-default installs)
#            ({HOME} is $HOME and {PWD} is the caller's cwd: neither has a twin
#            root override, so a caller confines a row that has no env var by
#            giving the run a scratch HOME / cwd — see the HIMMEL-3336 rule in
#   step     uninstall.sh step that acts on it (1-8; '-' for keep rows)
#   what     one line shown in the footprint
#   record   comma-separated provenance-ledger kinds install writes for this row
#            or 'none' when install records nothing for it. The reader also
#            accepts the older 8-column form (no record). A row whose `what`
#            says "removal pending" is listed for completeness: no step removes
#            it yet, so the printed REMOVE/KEEP verdict is the policy, not yet
